The '''1891–92 Scottish Football League''' was the second season of the [[Scottish Football League]] after its formation in 1890. A total of 12 clubs ([[Third Lanark A.C.|3rd LRV]], [[Abercorn F.C.|Abercorn]], [[Cambuslang F.C.|Cambuslang]], [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]], [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Leith Athletic F.C.|Leith Athletic]], [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], [[Renton F.C.|Renton]], [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] and [[Vale of Leven F.C.|Vale of Leven]]) took part in the competition. Dumbarton and Rangers were the defending champions having shared the title the previous season.<ref name="Graham"/>

The competition began with the first matches held on 15 August 1891 and concluded on 24 May 1892. The league was won by Dumbarton who won the title outright for the first time on 7 May 1892 after they drew 1–1 away to Abercorn in their final match.<ref name="ABC v DUM">{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/dumbarton/game.php?gameid=38031 |title=Abercorn 1 - 1 Dumbarton, Scottish League (07/05/1892) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>

In the close season after the league's successful first year, the Scottish Football League held its [[annual general meeting]]. As per the rules, the bottom three teams from season 1890–91 (St Mirren, Vale of Leven and Cowlairs) were put up for re-election to the league. Clyde and Leith Athletic both applied to join the league while league members agreed to increase the number of teams to 12. St Mirren, Vale of Leven, Clyde and Leith Athletic were all elected to join the league and would compete in the new season beginning on 15 August but Cowlairs failed re-election and instead became founding members of the [[Scottish Football Alliance]].<ref name="Graham"/><ref name="SFHA elections">{{cite web |url=http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/reelections.htm |title=Scottish Football League - Re-elections 1891-1951 |publisher=Scottish Football Historical Archive |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150414174453/http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/reelections.htm |archive-date=14 April 2015 |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> Renton competed for the first few months of the previous season but were expelled by the [[Scottish Football Association]] for professionalism however the club successfully appealed its suspension and was readmitted to the league for this season.<ref name="SFHA Renton">{{cite web |url=http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/expulsions.htm |title=Scottish Football League Expulsions 1890-1953 |publisher=Scottish Football Historical Archive |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150414220908/http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/expulsions.htm |archive-date=14 April 2015 |access-date=27 July 2019}}</ref>

==Season overview==
The league began on 15 August 1891. Both defending champions Dumbarton and Rangers opened the season with victories against Cambuslang (2–0)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/dumbarton/game.php?gameid=38014 |title=Cambuslang 0 - 2 Dumbarton, Scottish League (15/08/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> and Renton (4–1) respectively.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/rangers/game.php?gameid=80371 |title=Renton 1 - 4 Rangers, Scottish League (15/08/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> On the same day, Clyde defeated Vale of Leven 10–3 in what would be the joint highest-scoring game of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/clyde/game.php?gameid=71591 |title=Clyde 10 - 3 Vale of Leven, Scottish League (15/08/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>

Rangers suffered an early season set back when they lost the first [[Old Firm derby]] of the season to rivals Celtic 3–0 on 22 August<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/rangers/game.php?gameid=77053 |title=Celtic 3 - 0 Rangers, Scottish League (22/08/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> and, after a 3–1 defeat to Dumbarton two weeks later, they were effectively out of the running in 10th place with three defeats from their opening four games.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/rangers/game.php?gameid=38016 |title=Rangers 1 - 3 Dumbarton, Scottish League (05/09/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> Heart of Midlothian defeated Dumbarton 3–1 at [[Tynecastle Park]] on 29 August to take the early season lead two points clear at the top.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/hearts/game.php?gameid=19776 |title=Heart of Midlothian 3 - 1 Dumbarton, Scottish League (29/08/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>

They would stay there until 19 September when a 5–1 reverse at [[Boghead Park]] saw Dumbarton leapfrog them to go top.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/dumbarton/game.php?gameid=19779 |title=Dumbarton 5 - 1 Heart of Midlothian, Scottish League (19/09/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> However, a run of three straight wins – culminating in a 10–3 defeat of Clyde – saw Heart of Midlothian three points clear of Celtic, Dumbarton and Leith Athletic on 3 October.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/hearts/game.php?gameid=19782 |title=Clyde 3 - 10 Heart of Midlothian, Scottish League (03/10/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>

Dropping points to St Mirren and Vale of Leven allowed the chasing pack to catch up but it was Dumbarton who made the biggest impact. By the time they went top on 7 November after a tight 3–2 win against Renton, they had won five games in a row - a run that would extend well beyond the new year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/dumbarton/game.php?gameid=38022 |title=Renton 2 - 3 Dumbarton, Scottish League (07/11/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> On Boxing day they again defeated Renton 2–1 to move five points clear of Heart of Midlothian and 10 clear of third-placed Celtic but the Glasgow side had six games in hand, enough to catch and pass the league leaders.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/dumbarton/game.php?gameid=38026 |title=Dumbarton 2 - 1 Renton, Scottish League (26/12/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>

Dumbarton would play just two games in the new year before a crucial tie at home to Celtic on 23 April 1892. The Glasgow side had been unbeaten in all competitions after their opening day loss to Heart of Midlothian racking up 23 wins in 25 games – winning the [[Glasgow Cup]] and the [[1891–92 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] in the process – before a 2–1 loss away to Leith Athletic.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/celtic/game.php?gameid=77061 |title=Leith Athletic 2 - 1 Celtic, Scottish League (18/04/1892) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> That left Dumbarton on 32 points, one clear of Heart of Midlothian with a game in hand and six clear of Celtic who had two games in hand on the league leaders. [[John Miller (footballer, born 1870)|John Miller]] scored the only goal in front of 12,000 spectators at Boghead Park to put Dumbarton in pole position to claim the title.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sonsarchive.com/matchdetails.php?id=144 |title=Dumbarton 1-0 Celtic, Saturday, April 23rd, 1892 |publisher=Sons Archive |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=5 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190705112923/http://www.sonsarchive.com/matchdetails.php%3Fid%3D144 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

A 6–0 humbling of Rangers 11 days later – in which the league's top scorer [[Jack Bell (footballer, born 1869)|Jack Bell]] scored a hat-trick – put Dumbarton on the brink<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sonsarchive.com/matchdetails.php?id=146 |title=Dumbarton 6-0 Rangers, Wednesday, May 4th, 1892 |publisher=Sons Archive |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=21 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200821042748/http://sonsarchive.com/matchdetails.php?id=146 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and, in their final match of the season on 7 May, a 1–1 draw with Abercorn was enough to secure a second league title.<ref name="ABC v DUM"/> On the same day, Vale of Leven drew 1–1 with Renton in their final match as they finished bottom of the table, failing to win a single game throughout the league season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/valeofleven/game.php?gameid=88178 |title=Vale of Leven 1 - 1 Renton, Scottish League (07/05/1892) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>

At the league's annual general meeting on 3 June 1892, it was voted that the number of competing clubs would reduce from 12 to 10 for the next season. The bottom three clubs, St Mirren, Cambuslang and Vale of Leven, had to submit applications to rejoin the league for the next season. The league also received applications from four non-league clubs: [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], Cowlairs, [[Northern F.C.|Northern]] and [[St Bernard's F.C.|St Bernard's]]. In the election, St Mirren received the most votes and retained their league status meaning Cambuslang and Vale of Leven lost their league places.<ref name="SFHA elections"/>
